review_notes: Bangladesh is explicitly listed in Group II: tourist visa required without prior DIGEMIG consultation. The Embassy states a single-entry 30-day visa, extendable in Bolivia up to 90 days per calendar year, with Group II consular issuance within 24 hours after a complete application. The Group II visa is free except for specified nationalities (China/Hong Kong/Taiwan and Iran); Bangladesh is not among those exceptions. A separate USD52 first-border permit is exceptional and available only where there is no Bolivian diplomatic or consular representation near the applicant's country of residence. The New Delhi embassy's generic tariff page lists USD50 for tourism subject to reciprocity; the Bangladesh-specific Group II rule is more specific, so confirm any local charge with the competent mission.
notes: Bangladesh ordinary passport holders are Group II. Do not describe this as standard visa on arrival: the USD52 border permit is an exceptional route conditional on no nearby Bolivian mission.

review_notes: Cuba Travel states that a tourist visa is mandatory for visitors without Cuban residence, is single-entry, permits 90 days and may be extended for 90 more days; it identifies Chinese ordinary-passport holders as exempt. Bangladesh is not among the visa-exemption agreements listed by Bangladesh's Security Services Division. The official eVisa portal accepts online tourist-visa applications, requires a valid passport and email, and states a response within 72 business hours. Cuba Travel also requires a six-month passport, medical insurance, round-trip ticket, health declaration and D'Viajeros QR. The official portal does not publish one universal fee in the reviewed public guidance.
notes: Bangladesh ordinary passport holders require a tourist eVisa. Fee is channel-dependent and not published as one universal amount; verify the amount at the official checkout or competent consulate.

review_notes: The Embassy of Haiti states that tourists generally do not need a visa, passports must be valid at least six months, and USD10 is payable on arrival at the airport. Its visa-required list names Dominican Republic, Panama, Colombia, Cuba, Syria, Libya, Iran, Vietnam and Yemen; Bangladesh is not included. The Embassy's separate consular tariff page lists fees for tourist visas issued to applicants who require a visa; those consular fees are distinct from the USD10 airport arrival fee. notes: Do not label the USD10 airport arrival fee as a visa fee. No official maximum tourist stay was stated on the reviewed Embassy page.
